focus: Mechanism A - a gate in AGENTS.md that routes a write request into workflow steps
noveltyJustification: The Cursor reach gap, the shipped/local split and the per-gate exemption pattern are new; the fact that AGENTS.md is widely loaded was already known.
keyQuestions: For each candidate mechanism (AGENTS.md gate, shared step reference, hook injection, template and validate.sh enforcement, advisor-driven command invocation), what does it cost and what does it break?
ruledOut: Proposing that Cursor be given a full AGENTS.md copy
Proposing the gate be written inside the repo-local block

graphEvents.label: Six of seven runtimes read AGENTS.md
Cursor reads only a generated Gate 1 pointer
AGENTS.md is a shipped product surface
Existing gates route away to a file

findings.label: Six of seven runtimes load the root AGENTS.md natively
Cursor receives only a 2257-byte routing rule and a generated Gate 1 pointer block
AGENTS.md lines 1-295 are shipped by Skilled and only 296-300 are repository-owned
Resident cost is about 6.8k tokens per session versus 12.4k bytes for REPO RULES loaded only on writes
Every existing AGENTS.md gate routes away to a skill or rule file rather than embedding steps
A write-time routing gate would be the fourth stop-and-ask surface on the same event
The trivial-edit exemptions are written per gate and would need a third written exception
A gate is instruction not enforcement and the repo's own evidence standard says so
REPO RULES.md already provides the action-matched router shape at a write-only load point

ruledOutDetailed.direction: Proposing that Cursor be given a full AGENTS.md copy
ruledOutDetailed.reason: Divergence between runtime mirrors is treated as drift; the Cursor README names one generator for its single generated block.

ruledOutDetailed.direction: Proposing the gate be written inside the repo-local block
ruledOutDetailed.reason: That fixes this repository and ships nothing, which cannot answer a question about every chat session.
